slideDifferences.nativeText:
Talking about habits in the past leads us to use simple past tense structure; though, it is necessary to work with used to.
TO CONSIDER
Used to is a fixed expression that comes before a verb in simple form. 
 If the sentence has the auxiliary DID, used to goes in simple form.
Other useful expressions: but not anymore / Back in my childhood / When I was a child / When I was younger etc. 
Used to can be used in simple present tense to talk about customs people have. E.G. She is used to read the newspaper in the mornings.
Used to
John used to attend dancing classes all nights.
Did John use to attend dancing classes all nights?
I used to make cakes back in my school days.
Did you use to make cakes back in your school day?

texts: Language bricks
Talking about habits in the past leads us to use simple past tense structure; though, it is necessary to work with used to.
TO CONSIDER
Used to is a fixed expression that comes before a verb in simple form.
If the sentence has the auxiliary DID, used to goes in simple form.
Other useful expressions: but not anymore / Back in my childhood / When I was a child / When I was younger etc.
Used to can be used in simple present tense to talk about customs people have. E.G. She is used to read the newspaper in the mornings.
Used to
John used to attend dancing classes all nights.
Did John use to attend dancing classes all nights?
I used to make cakes back in my school days.
Did you use to make cakes back in your school day?

texts: Functional English
Language Targets
Aspects
Examples
Talk about infancy experiences.
We used to have a baseball team in our street back in the 80s.
State old bad habits.
John used to smoke a lot but he stopped a few months ago.
Define people’s old conditions.
Jake looks great, He used to wear messy hair but not anymore.
Express customs people have
They are used to drink coffee only in the mornings.
When using past simple to talk about habits, we may be talking about different aspects or functions.
TO CONSIDER
Time phrases are very important, no matter the function or aspect covered; sometimes, they determine the context

texts: Memories!
I always remember my childhood. I used to spend hours
with my friends nearby the river swimming,
playing and sometimes camping.
We used to go there almost every
Saturday to play at the tree house and to listen to
good music. I have to admit that we used to be very

noisy kids; however, we used to be good kids and we never made anything terrible…well, we used to ring doorbells to our neighbors so we were not angels either. I’d wish those times to be back, kids now do not enjoy life since technology has overtaken them; I truly think we had the greatest childhood.
C. Read the following paragraph and state if the sentences are true (T) or false (F). After that, read the paragraph aloud to your teacher.
1.  He never remembers his childhood.		(T) (F)
2. He used to spend hours near the lake.	(T) (F)
3. They used to go camping too.			(T) (F)
4. They used to go there every Saturday.	(T) (F)
5.  They used to read books at the tree house.	(T) (F)
6.  They used to be bad kids.				(T) (F)
7.   They didn’t use to ring doorbells.			(T) (F)
8.   He considers they had the greatest childhood.	(T) (F)

good music. I have to admit that we used to be very
noisy kids; however, we used to be good kids and we never made anything terrible…well, we used to ring doorbells to our neighbors so we were not angels either.
